title: Settling a Building Automation Service Plan in One Payment, and the Payment the Owner Puts Through
content:
# Settling a Building Automation Service Plan in One Payment, and the Payment the Owner Puts Through

## The settlement

A building owner who wants an automation service plan put back in order settles it in one payment, and the sum required is worked out from the plan's own billing history. The sum required to settle a plan is fixed only after every hour of controls support work the plan's included support hours do not cover stands invoiced on the plan's billing history.

## Putting the payment through

The payment against a plan under the Building Automation Service Plans is the building owner's own act. The desk unlocks the tool `record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. One call applies one payment of their own money to the named plan, reduces what they owe under that plan by exactly that amount, and files the payment in the plan's billing history under today's office date. The owner can see the payment and the reduced balance on the plan from that moment.

## What is given at the call

- `plan_id` — the reference number of the automation service plan the money is being paid against, read from the automation service plan lookup before the call.
- `payment_amount_usd` — the money actually being paid, in USD, recorded positive and to 2 decimal places.
- `payment_method` — how the owner is sending the money, one of exactly four settled values:

| Value | When it applies |
|---|---|
| `check` | the owner is posting or hand-delivering a paper cheque drawn on the company account |
| `ach` | the owner is pushing the money from their own bank by electronic transfer through the automated clearing house |
| `credit_card` | the owner is putting the payment on a company card over the telephone or through the portal |
| `wire` | the owner is sending same-day cleared funds by bank wire |

## What comes back

A confirmation sentence in plain text naming the filed payment entry's reference, the amount paid in USD to two decimal places, the plan it was applied to, the method it came in by and the balance still owed under the plan afterwards. The sentence being returned at all is what indicates the payment was applied; no separate status flag is sent back.

## Contract questions

**Whose money is it?** The building owner's own: the tool is the owner's to run once it is handed over.

**What does the plan's balance do?** What the owner owes under that plan falls by exactly the amount paid, and the payment stands in the plan's billing history under today's office date.
